newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.S., EU see solution to grain tariff row.
newsitem.headline: U.S., EU see solution to grain tariff row.

text.p: The United States and the European Union said on Thursday they saw good prospects for a solution to their long-running row over EU grain tariffs.
Trade sources said officials from both powers told a meeting of the World Trade Organisation's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) that a settlement seemed in sight.
But at the same time the United States said it was going ahead with a new request for WTO panel to adjudicate in the spat pending a positive outcome.
EU diplomat Ian Wilkinson said Brussels could not agree to a panel immediately, saying the two sides were working for a solution which was "within sight", according to the sources.
U.S. representative Andrew Shoyer said Washington and Brussels were making "good progress" towards an accord and he hoped to be able to report one was reached at the next DSB meeting on April 30.
He said if that was the case, the United States would be able to withdraw its request for a panel -- which otherwise, under WTO rules, would have been created automatically.
The row, which broke out in 1995, centres on a tariff system Washington says violates agreements under the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of trade negotiations.
The United States has filed and then withdrawn panel requests in the WTO at least twice so far.
Last month the EU agreed to change its rice import system and to open a new tariff quota for U.S. malting barley, both effective from May 1.
This appeared to have resolved the dispute, but Washington, apparently fearing possible backsliding, clearly decided to keep up the pressure through the WTO.

U.S. officials say they have been concerned that the EU has not yet published either a new cumulative recovery system for rice imports, which allows traders to reclaim excess import duties, nor the malting barley quota.
But the EU says the decisions had been taken by member states and could not be unravelled.
